title: SimulationConfig
description: Shared $defs describing HOW one synthetic simulation was generated, organized by the generation functions that don't change: geometry / cell_model / substrate / activation / electrodes / backend / label_policy. Like common.schema.json this is NOT a document format on its own — it has no document validator and nothing is written to disk in this shape; synthetic_bank $refs these definitions and stores one JSON-encoded object per column in its `simulations/` group. WHY IT EXISTS: synthetic_bank 1.1 recorded generation parameters as flat per-trace columns (fibrosis_density, stim_edge, electrode_height_mm), each of which silently assumed the Phase-1 setup — a uniformly-random substrate, a planar-edge stimulus on a 2D patch. Every new cell model, substrate type, or stimulus protocol forced either new trace columns or semantic drift in existing ones. Here each generation function is one type-discriminated object, so a new variant extends its function without touching the trace columns or the bank's top-level shape. Each object mirrors the corresponding strategy Protocol in synthetic-egm-pipeline's simulate/specs.py, and the `type` discriminator values match that module's Literal values exactly — the producer's dataclass and this schema are two views of one contract, so a rename in either is a coordinated change. Design: intracardiac-platform/project/investigations/synthetic_bank_schema_design.md. SCOPE: everything here describes ONE simulation. What a multi-simulation SWEEP varied — the theta-spec — is bank-scoped and lives in generation_params.schema.json, referenced from synthetic_bank's root attrs rather than its per-simulation group.

Geometry.title: Geometry
Geometry.description: The tissue domain. Phase 1.5 ships the 2D patch; 3D variants (atrial mesh, cylinder) extend this union without changing anything that references it. Positions elsewhere in the config are coordinate arrays whose length follows the active variant's dimensionality — nothing downstream hard-codes 2 or 3.

Patch2DGeometry.title: Patch2DGeometry
Patch2DGeometry.description: A 2D square tissue patch with uniform fiber orientation. Mirrors specs.Patch2DGeometry.

size_mm.description: Physical edge length of the square patch in mm. Phase 1 = 40.

dr_mm.description: Spatial discretization step in mm; mesh size per edge is round(size_mm / dr_mm). Phase 1 = 0.25.

fiber_angle_rad.description: Fiber orientation in radians (0 = along +x, pi/2 = along +y).

anisotropy_ratio.description: Conduction-velocity ratio CV_along / CV_across; 1 = isotropic. Prescriptive — the backend configures its diffusion tensor so the realized ratio matches (CV scales with sqrt(D), so D_along / D_across = anisotropy_ratio^2).

CellModel.title: CellModel
CellModel.description: The cellular electrophysiology model. Phase 1.5's headline realism lever is the move from the phenomenological Aliev-Panfilov model to Courtemanche, a human-atrial ionic model — hence both variants, not just the new one: a bank generated under either must remain readable and self-describing.

CourtemancheCellModel.title: CourtemancheCellModel
CourtemancheCellModel.description: Courtemanche-Ramirez-Nattel human atrial ionic model. Time is already physical (ms), so no model-time calibration constant is needed — unlike Aliev-Panfilov.

params.description: Model parameter overrides applied on top of the backend's defaults, as {name: value} — typically ionic conductance scalings (e.g. g_CaL_scale, g_K1_scale). Deliberately open: which conductances are worth varying is an experimental question the phase's screening answers, and pinning a fixed key set here would force a schema bump every time that answer changes. The bank-scoped theta-spec (generation_params.schema.json) points INTO this object by path when a knob is being swept.

AlievPanfilovCellModel.title: AlievPanfilovCellModel
AlievPanfilovCellModel.description: Aliev-Panfilov phenomenological model — the Phase-1 baseline, kept so v1 banks stay describable and the A/B against Courtemanche is expressible.

ap_time_unit_ms.description: Calibration constant mapping one model time unit to physical milliseconds. Aliev-Panfilov is non-dimensional in time, so every duration in the run is expressed through this constant; it is meaningless for ionic models, which is exactly why it lives on this variant rather than on the backend.

params.description: Model parameter overrides ({name: value}) on top of the backend's defaults.

Substrate.title: Substrate
Substrate.description: The fibrosis (or other substrate) pattern. Phase 1.5 ships uniform-random; interstitial / patchy / compact / heterogeneous-mix variants extend this union. Note what this object is NOT: it holds the REQUESTED pattern parameters, while what the draw actually produced is separate (see SubstrateSummary) — the two differ through grid discretization, and conflating them was one of the flaws in the flat-column layout.

UniformRandomFibrosis.title: UniformRandomFibrosis
UniformRandomFibrosis.description: I.i.d. nodal fibrosis: each interior mesh node is marked non-conductive with probability `density`. Matches Nezlobinsky 2021 / Okenov 2024. Mirrors specs.UniformRandomFibrosis.

density.description: Target fibrotic-node fraction. 0.0 is exactly healthy; propagation tends to fail above ~0.6 (Nezlobinsky 2021), and Phase 1 sampled [0, 0.5]. The bound is the physical one (a fraction), not the useful one — the useful range is a producer-side sampling decision, not a contract.

SubstrateSummary.title: SubstrateSummary
SubstrateSummary.description: What the substrate draw actually realized, as opposed to what was requested. Separated from the Substrate object because a realized quantity is an OUTPUT of generation: the realized density differs from the requested one through grid discretization, and a variant with no scalar density at all (patchy, compact) still reports something here. Open key set — each substrate variant summarizes itself. WATCH (2026-07-30): this is one flat object shared by every substrate type, which holds while uniform-random is the only one. Once interstitial / patchy / compact land, their meaningful summaries diverge — cluster-size distribution, strand length, patch count — and a shared bag of optional keys stops describing any of them well. At that point this likely becomes a discriminated union keyed to the substrate variant, the same shape Substrate already has. Deliberately not done now: with one variant, a union of one is structure without information.

realized_density.description: Fraction of mesh nodes actually marked non-conductive after the draw.

n_fibrotic_nodes.description: Count of non-conductive nodes in the realized mask.

Activation.title: Activation
Activation.description: How the activation wave is initiated. Replaces synthetic_bank 1.1's `stim_edge` enum, which could only ever name one of four edges of a 2D patch — a point source needs a coordinate, and a paced protocol needs timings. Phase 1.5 ships planar-edge (Wave 1, today's behavior), plus point and S1-S2 (Wave 2, SEP7); a pacing train arrives in Phase 4 as another variant here.

PlanarEdgeActivation.title: PlanarEdgeActivation
PlanarEdgeActivation.description: A thin strip of voltage applied at one or more mesh edges; the wave propagates inward. Mirrors specs.PlanarEdgeStimulus, with one deliberate difference: `edges` is a LIST where the producer's Phase-1 dataclass carries a single `edge`. Today's single-edge behavior is the one-element list, so the Wave-1 migration writes ['top'] and SEP6's multi-edge feature needs no schema change — the alternative (adding a field in Wave 2) would have put a contracts bump in the middle of the feature wave.

edges.description: Which edge(s) fire. One entry reproduces Phase-1 behavior; several give the propagation-direction variety that drives morphology diversity.

voltage.description: Stimulus amplitude in the cell model's voltage units (not mV — the models are dimensionless or model-specific here).

time_model_units.description: When the stimulus fires, in the backend's model time units.

strip_thickness.description: Strip thickness in mesh cells. A thicker strip is more reliable at triggering propagation on a fibrotic substrate.

PointActivation.title: PointActivation
PointActivation.description: A point (or small ball) stimulus at a coordinate — the variant that flat `stim_edge` could not express at all. Gives curved wavefronts and off-axis propagation.

position_mm.description: Stimulus location in mm, in the geometry's coordinate frame. Length follows the active Geometry variant: [x, y] on a 2D patch, [x, y, z] on a 3D mesh.

radius_mm.description: Radius of the stimulated ball in mm. Omit for a single-node stimulus.

voltage.description: Stimulus amplitude in the cell model's voltage units.

time_model_units.description: When the stimulus fires, in the backend's model time units.

S1S2Activation.title: S1S2Activation
S1S2Activation.description: An S1-S2 protocol: a train of conditioning stimuli followed by a premature one at a coupling interval, used to probe refractoriness. The stimulus itself is a nested SingleShotActivation, so an S1-S2 can be driven from an edge or a point without this variant restating either one's fields. Its `time_model_units` is IGNORED — protocol timing comes from the intervals below — and its `voltage` applies to every stimulus in the train. PROVISIONAL: this variant exists now so SEP7 can implement it in Wave 2 without a contracts bump, but the field set is the schema author's reading of the protocol, not a producer design that has been built. Confirm against SEP7's implementation before any bank is written with it; extending it later is additive.

site.description: The stimulus each S1 and the S2 delivers — an ordinary single-shot activation, whose own timing field is ignored in favour of the protocol's intervals.

s2_interval_ms.description: Coupling interval between the last S1 and the premature S2 — the knob that probes refractoriness.

n_s1.description: Number of S1 stimuli delivered before the S2.

Electrodes.title: Electrodes
Electrodes.description: Electrode placement AND the realized per-pair detail for one simulation. This is where synthetic_bank 1.1's per-trace `electrode_row` / `electrode_height_mm` columns moved to: those values are per electrode pair, and every trace from one simulation shares the same placement, so storing them once per simulation and indexing by pair_index removes the repetition without losing anything.

CenteredGrid2DElectrodes.title: CenteredGrid2DElectrodes
CenteredGrid2DElectrodes.description: A rows x cols grid centred on a 2D patch, with consecutive within-row electrodes forming bipolar pairs (so a 5x5 grid yields 5 * 4 = 20 pairs). Mirrors specs.CenteredGrid2D. Height is sampled per simulation, so `height_mm` here is the realized value for THIS simulation, not a configured range — the range is a producer-side sampling decision recorded in the theta-spec when it is being swept.

n_cols.description: Grid columns. At least 2 — a bipolar pair needs two electrodes in a row.

spacing_mm.description: Intra-row and inter-row electrode spacing in mm.

height_mm.description: Realized electrode height above the tissue surface for this simulation, in mm. A strong driver of EGM amplitude and morphology, which is why it is a candidate sweep knob.

positions_mm.description: (n_electrodes, D) electrode positions in mm, in the geometry's coordinate frame; D follows the active Geometry variant. Ordered row-major, so index = row * n_cols + col, which is what `pairs` indexes into.

pairs.description: The realized bipolar pairs, in trace order. A trace in the bank carries a `pair_index` into this list rather than repeating any of it per trace.

BipolarPair.title: BipolarPair
BipolarPair.description: One realized bipolar electrode pair. Everything a consumer previously read from the per-trace columns lives here.

pair_index.description: Position of this pair in the list; the value a trace stores to reference it. Explicit rather than implied by array order so a filtered or reordered view can't silently renumber pairs.

electrode_indices.description: The (a, b) indices into positions_mm whose difference forms the bipolar signal.

electrode_row.description: Grid row this pair sits in. Was a per-trace column in 1.1.

height_mm.description: Height of this pair above the tissue in mm. Was a per-trace column in 1.1. Equal to the placement's height_mm for a flat grid, but kept per pair so a non-planar placement (a 3D catheter) needs no schema change.

midpoint_mm.description: Midpoint of the two electrodes in mm — the point a bipolar trace is usually attributed to when relating it to the substrate beneath it.

Backend.title: Backend
Backend.description: The simulator that ran this simulation, plus its run-level capture knobs. Phase 1.5 ships Finitewave; openCARP / TorchCor would extend this union. Recorded because a trace's fidelity is not reproducible from the physics alone — sample rate and oversampling shape what reached the bank.

version.description: Finitewave version string that produced the simulation.

output_fs_hz.description: On-disk sample rate after downsampling. Phase 1 = 1000 to match IAFDB; synthetic and real must share a rate for lag-based features to be comparable.

capture_oversample.description: The backend captures at capture_oversample * output_fs_hz and the runner downsamples. Recorded because it determines whether the on-disk trace is anti-aliased by oversampling margin rather than by a filter.

dt_model_units.description: Solver time step in the model's time units.

params.description: Additional backend knobs ({name: value}), e.g. diffusion. Open for the same reason the cell-model params are: which solver knobs get swept is an experimental question, and the theta-spec points into this object by path.

LabelPolicy.title: LabelPolicy
LabelPolicy.description: The rule that turned a realized substrate into the integer label a trace carries. Stored per simulation rather than per trace: the trace keeps a plain int (so the classifier's input contract never changes shape), and this object plus LabelNames is what makes that int interpretable. A new label family — fibrotic type, neighbourhood composition, multiclass severity — is a new variant here and changes nothing downstream of the label column.

GlobalDensityLabel.title: GlobalDensityLabel
GlobalDensityLabel.description: Labels every trace in the simulation by the WHOLE patch's realized fibrosis density against a threshold. Mirrors label_policy.GlobalDensityLabel. Note the implication, which is a known limitation rather than a bug: every trace in a simulation gets the same label regardless of where its electrode pair sat. Class names are NOT carried here — LabelNames owns them, so a bank states each class's meaning exactly once.

thresholds.description: Ascending realized whole-patch density cut points. N thresholds produce N+1 classes, so a binary healthy/fibrotic policy is a single-element array and a Phase-2 severity policy is several — no new variant, no contracts bump. Class k is the band between thresholds[k-1] and thresholds[k]; class names live in LabelNames, which already maps any number of labels and is the single place a class is named.

LocalDensityLabel.title: LocalDensityLabel
LocalDensityLabel.description: Labels each trace by the realized fibrosis density within a radius of its own pair midpoint — so traces from one simulation can disagree, which is the point. Mirrors label_policy.LocalDensityLabel. Class names are NOT carried here — LabelNames owns them, so a bank states each class's meaning exactly once.

radius_mm.description: Radius around the pair midpoint over which density is measured. Sets what 'local' means, and is worth recording because a result only reproduces at the same radius.

thresholds.description: Ascending local density cut points. N thresholds produce N+1 classes, so a binary healthy/fibrotic policy is a single-element array and a Phase-2 severity policy is several — no new variant, no contracts bump. Class k is the band between thresholds[k-1] and thresholds[k]; class names live in LabelNames, which already maps any number of labels and is the single place a class is named.

LabelNames.title: LabelNames
LabelNames.description: Map from integer label to human-readable class name, e.g. {"0": "healthy", "1": "fibrotic"}. Keys are stringified integers because JSON object keys are strings. Carried alongside the policy so a bank is self-describing: without it the label column is an int with no stated meaning, and the meaning has already changed once (density scalar -> binary class) and will change again at multiclass severity.

Edge.title: Edge
Edge.description: A mesh edge, in the backend's naming convention: top = smallest axis-0 index, bottom = largest axis-0, left = smallest axis-1, right = largest axis-1. Electrode coordinates use the same axis convention. Defined once and $ref'd by every variant that names an edge, so a single-shot stimulus and a paced protocol cannot end up disagreeing about what 'top' means.

PositionMm.title: PositionMm
PositionMm.description: A coordinate in millimetres, in the geometry's frame. Length follows the active Geometry variant: [x, y] on a 2D patch, [x, y, z] on a 3D mesh. Defined once so stimulus sites, electrode positions and pair midpoints stay dimensionally consistent with each other.

SingleShotActivation.title: SingleShotActivation
SingleShotActivation.description: An activation that fires once — the stimulus shapes a protocol can deliver repeatedly. Exists so S1S2Activation can reference a real activation variant rather than a parallel set of 'site' objects duplicating their fields; the union excludes protocol variants, which is what stops a protocol nesting another protocol.
